stories.notes: Complex multi-platform live preview feature with empty AC and no existing spec. Needs openspec to elaborate requirements and define acceptance criteria, then speckit to harden testability, security, and edge cases. Both agents warranted due to complexity and lack of baseline specification.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — live preview does not exist. Attachment points are the content hook, context provider, and service layer. VCs derived from description's three named behaviors (real-time preview, no full page reload, no manual republish) since ACs are empty.

Openspec provided empty ACs, so I authored the full list from scratch based on the story description's three named behaviors (real-time preview, no full page reload, no manual republish) and the file paths indicating the integration surface (hooks, context, service, components). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: file contents were unavailable, so criteria are derived solely from the description, title, and paths — not from actual code analysis. Criteria may need adjustment once implementation details are known. AC-1 through AC-3 cover the three core behaviors. AC-4/AC-5 cover connection lifecycle edge cases. AC-6 covers malformed data. AC-7 covers rapid-update race conditions. AC-8/AC-9 cover security. AC-10/AC-11 cover accessibility. AC-12 covers UX clarity. AC-13 covers multi-user isolation. AC-14 covers content type breadth. AC-15 covers graceful degradation.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline breakdown detected. Openspec was assigned to elaborate requirements but its contribution shows acceptanceChanged=false and notes confirm ACs remained empty — it produced no elaborated acceptance criteria. Speckit then compensated by authoring all 15 ACs from scratch, but explicitly caveats that file contents were unavailable and criteria were derived solely from title, description, and file paths rather than actual code analysis. While speckit's ACs appear comprehensive in coverage (core behaviors, edge cases, security, accessibility, multi-user isolation, graceful degradation), the entire specification rests on inference without code-level grounding. Both agents did not add non-overlapping value in the intended manner — openspec was effectively a no-op and speckit carried the full load blind. Human review is required to validate that the 15 ACs align with actual implementation surfaces and to determine whether openspec should be re-run with code access enabled.
